1 Corinthians 15:10 is a powerful foundation for a BibleFuel Studio video. I would build it around one central message:

“I AM NOT SELF-MADE. I AM GRACE-MADE.”

The verse says (KJV):

> “But by the grace of God I am what I am: and his grace which was bestowed upon me was not in vain; but I laboured more abundantly than they all: yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.”

## BibleFuel Studio — Cinematic Script

TITLE: GRACE MADE ME | 1 CORINTHIANS 15:10

90-second devotional

9:16 cinematic

Afro-soul + gospel orchestral

[Divine Word](https://images.example.com/divine-word?purpose=inline)

# GRACE MADE ME

**Scripture: 1 Corinthians 15:10**

### Scene 1 — The Hook (0:00–0:12)

*Visual: A man standing alone in the darkness. A narrow beam of golden light falls across his face.*

**Narrator (deep, emotional voice):**

"Look at me today…

You may see strength.

You may see success.

You may see someone who has everything figured out.

But you don't know the battles that brought me here."

### Scene 2 — The Revelation (0:12–0:27)

*Visual: Flashbacks of a man kneeling in prayer, struggling through difficult moments, then rising again.*

**Narrator:**

"There were nights I almost gave up.

Doors that closed in my face.

Mistakes I thought would define me forever.

But there was something greater than my weakness…

**The grace of God.**"

### Scene 3 — The Scripture (0:27–0:46)

*Visual: Sunlight breaks through the clouds. A figure stands with arms raised as the music begins to swell.*

**Narrator (stronger, deliberate):**

"The Apostle Paul declared:

'But by the grace of God I am what I am: and his grace which was bestowed upon me was not in vain…'

**First Corinthians, chapter fifteen, verse ten.**"

### Scene 4 — The Transformation (0:46–1:05)

*Visual: A cinematic montage of a mother caring for her children, a young man working late, a woman graduating, and a worshipper lifting their hands.*

**Narrator (with conviction):**

"Grace did not mean Paul stopped working.

Grace gave his labour a purpose.

He worked with everything he had…

But he never took the glory.

Because behind every achievement,

Behind every second chance,

Behind every victory…

**God's grace was working.**"

### Scene 5 — The Declaration (1:05–1:20)

*Visual: The central character walks into brilliant morning light. The instrumental rises into a victorious gospel crescendo.*

**Narrator (bold and uplifting):**

"So when they ask me how I survived…

How I kept going…

How I became who I am today…

My answer will remain the same:

**NOT BY MY STRENGTH.**

**NOT BY MY WISDOM.**

**BUT BY THE GRACE OF GOD!**"

### Scene 6 — The Final Message (1:20–1:30)

*Visual: Beautiful golden sunrise over a peaceful landscape. Music softens to piano and choir.*

**Narrator (gentle, intimate):**

"I am not self-made.

I am grace-made.

And His grace upon my life…

**Will not be in vain.**"

*Final screen: 1 CORINTHIANS 15:10 — BY THE GRACE OF GOD I AM WHAT I AM.*

## Music and sound direction

I would give this video a beautiful instrumental progression rather than playing a single background track throughout.

[Testimonials | Miller Piano](https://images.example.com/piano?purpose=inline)

0:00–0:27 | Emotional reflection

Soft piano, distant cello, atmospheric textures, and a subtle heartbeat-like percussion. Keep the narration intimate.

0:27–1:05 | Grace revealed

Add warm strings, rich gospel chords, restrained Afro-soul percussion, and gentle choir harmonies beneath the Scripture.

1:05–1:30 | Victorious declaration

Powerful orchestral drums, tasteful gángan accents, gospel choir, and uplifting brass. Drop the instrumentals briefly before “BUT BY THE GRACE OF GOD!”

## What would make this especially powerful?

For BibleFuel, I recommend using two contrasting voices: a mature, deep male narrator delivering the personal testimony, and a gentle female voice reading the opening words of Paul's declaration. Then an ensemble of adults and children can softly repeat:

> "By His grace… I am what I am."

That becomes the emotional signature of the production.
